issues.legal_issue: A timely tender of rent that the landlord refuses can support subsequent deposits with the rent authority, and deposits made within the applicable time do not establish the rent default required for eviction.
material_facts: Rent was payable monthly, and no contract fixed a different payment time.
The tenant sent the rent for one month by money order within the applicable time, but the landlord refused it.
The tenant later deposited that month's rent with the rent authority and deposited the rents for subsequent months; the court found those subsequent deposits were not late.
The High Court treated the deposits as invalid because it considered them unpreceded by a valid tender, despite finding that the initial money-order tender was timely.
issues.conclusion: The initial tender was valid, the High Court's basis for treating the deposits as invalid was incorrect, and there was no default of the kind required for eviction. The appeal was allowed and the eviction suit dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4, 13(1)(i), 21 and 22 of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1955, a tenant's eviction for rent default requires the specified pattern of defaults. A timely tender refused by the landlord permits the tenant to deposit rent with the rent authority; after a valid tender is refused, Section 21(4A) allows deposits for subsequent months without further tenders. The court relied on the statutory requirements and did not cite an earlier case.

rule.if: appeal_from_eviction_decree and monthly_rent_payable and timely_initial_rent_tender and landlord_refused_initial_tender and rent_deposited_with_authority and subsequent_rent_deposits_timely

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree ordering eviction for rent default.
predicates.monthly_rent_payable: The tenancy requires rent to be paid monthly.
predicates.timely_initial_rent_tender: The tenant tendered the rent for a month within the applicable payment time.
predicates.landlord_refused_initial_tender: The landlord refused the timely tender of rent.
predicates.rent_deposited_with_authority: The tenant deposited the refused rent with the rent authority.
predicates.subsequent_rent_deposits_timely: The tenant deposited the rents for subsequent months within the applicable time.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an eviction decree in a monthly-rent tenancy, and the tenant timely tenders rent, the landlord refuses it, and the tenant makes the required timely deposits, the tenant is not in default for eviction.

issues.legal_issue: After a landlord refuses a valid tender of rent, subsequent monthly rents may be deposited with the rent authority within the applicable deposit period rather than the deadline for tendering rent to the landlord.
material_facts: The landlord refused a timely tender of rent for one month.
The tenant thereafter deposited rent for subsequent months with the rent authority without making further tenders to the landlord.
The landlord argued that the later deposits had to be made by the deadline for payment of rent to the landlord; the court rejected that construction of Sections 21 and 22.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent deposits were not required to meet the deadline for tendering rent to the landlord; the applicable deposit period governs.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 21 and 22 of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1955, read together, permit deposits for subsequent months without further tenders after refusal of a valid tender and apply the statutory time limit for deposits with the rent authority. The court relied on the plain reading of those provisions and cited no earlier case.

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree ordering eviction for rent default.
predicates.landlord_refused_valid_rent_tender: The landlord refused a tender of rent that was made within the applicable time.
predicates.subsequent_rents_deposited_with_authorit: The tenant deposited rents for later months with the rent authority after the refusal.

issues.definition: When a landlord refuses a valid rent tender in an eviction appeal and the tenant deposits later rents with the rent authority, those later deposits are governed by the authority deposit period.
